subject: Recap & next steps: Quantum Retail deployment topology and SLOs
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@quantumretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Recap & next steps: Quantum Retail deployment topology and SLOs

Hi Amanda —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we’re all aligned and have clear next steps. Please holler if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Checkout latency spikes during peak promo windows (20% of sessions seeing >2.5s response for recommendations).
- Cost unpredictability with current inference provider under scale; want better per-token/unit economics and visibility.
- Security/compliance: data residency in us-east required and SOC-2 evidence for vendor evaluation.

Primary goals discussed:
- Latency SLO: 95th pct latency <= 800ms for 512-token recommendation requests (p99 objective TBD in benchmarking).
- Throughput: baseline 400 concurrent active sessions (peak bursts to ~1,200) with steady-state batch efficiency.
- Model requirements: transformer-based reranker + 7B dense generation model for personalized copy; ability to pin model versions and fallback to quantized variants.

Proposed deployment topology (high level):
- Dedicated pool in us-east-1 (Redwood Dedicated) with autoscaling policy: target utilization 60-70%, burst capacity to handle promo spikes.
- Smart routing: low-latency region routing to keep green traffic in us-east; automatic fallback to smaller quantized model when cold-starts or capacity constrained.
- Prefix/KV cache for session contexts to reduce token costs and keep tail latency low.

Action items we agreed:
1) Redwood to share a short topology diagram + SLO runbook (attached: redwood-deploy-topology-v1.pdf). Marcus will include configuration suggestions for autoscaling and caching.
2) Quantum Retail to provide a representative request trace and a 24h peak-day log sample (you mentioned security will share via the secure upload link).
3) We will run a quick perf baseline (1–2 days) using your trace against the proposed setup; initial target: validate 95th<=800ms at baseline load.
4) Procurement touchpoint: Grace to introduce standard pricing/commit options and provide draft SOW.

Proposed timeline:
- Nov 30: Quantum provides request trace + sample dataset.
- Dec 2: Redwood runs baseline perf and returns a short report.
- Dec 6: Joint sync to review results and finalize committed capacity recommendation.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-topology-v1.pdf (topology + autoscale hints), quantum-eval-promptset.csv (example prompts you can confirm).

Thanks — looking forward to progressing.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0147

From: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@quantumretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Javier Morales <javier.morales@quantumretail.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Quantum Retail deployment topology and SLOs

Thanks Soojin — this matches my notes and looks good. A couple clarifications: 

- The 400 concurrent sessions is conservative for steady-state; during a flash sale we’ve seen ~1,400 concurrent recommendation renders (that’s why the burst behavior is critical). If your baseline run can hit 1,200 with acceptable degradations we’ll be pleased.
- For p99 we’re willing to accept a soft target of <1.6s if the 95th is under 800ms and we can see cost savings vs current provider.
- SOC-2 evidence: I’ll ask security to package the relevant reports and upload to the secure link you provide.

We’ll upload a 48-hour sample trace by end of day Nov 30. Also cc’ing Javier (CTO) so he can review the initial topology doc — Javier, feel free to add any infra constraints.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the perf run.

—Amanda
VP Product, Quantum Retail
Amanda.Cole@quantumretail.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@quantumretail.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:18:00 +0000
Subject: Perf baseline plan and quantization options

Amanda / team —

Following up with the technical runbook we discussed. Summary below and attached a one-page table in the PDF for quick reference.

Perf baseline plan (1–2 day run):
- Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1, 8xA100-80GB equivalent nodes for initial runs (we'll simulate both steady-state 400 concurrency and burst to 1,200).
- Models: full-precision 7B generation model (vanilla) and an int8-quantized variant for fallback. We'll also test a 3B distilled reranker model for ranking steps.
- Requests: use your 48h trace replay; synthetic burst traffic to validate autoscale reaction time.
- Metrics to collect: 95/99 latencies, p50, mean tokens/sec, tail CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, per-request token cost estimate.

SLO calibration notes:
- Target: 95th <= 800ms at baseline 400 concurrent requests with KV cache warming.
- Burst tolerance: during a 5–10 minute flash spike to 1,200 concurrent sessions, acceptable p95 degradation up to 1.2s if cost per request remains below threshold X (we'll compute threshold after baseline).
- Cold-starts: expect higher p99; propose warm-pool strategy for critical route endpoints to avoid long tails.

Topology specifics:
- Fronting LB -> routing policy (latency-first) -> dedicated inference pool -> cache tier (Redis KV) co-located in same AZ -> metrics/trace sink to Redwood Console + your Datadog.
- Failover: automatic fallback to quantized model in cross-Z capacity-pressure scenarios.

Next steps from our side:
- Run baseline as soon as we have the trace (ETA: Dec 2 report).
- Share perf CSV + short runbook (attached in redwood-deploy-topology-v1.pdf).

If this looks correct, I’ll kick off the job tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Marcus
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Amanda Cole <amanda.cole@quantumretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Javier Morales <javier.morales@quantumretail.com>, procure@quantumretail.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 18:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Perf baseline plan and quantization options

Perfect — thanks Marcus. We’ve uploaded the 48h trace to the secure folder and notified security to share SOC-2 artifacts. Please proceed with the baseline; we’ll look out for the Dec 2 report.

One procurement note: we prefer a 12-month committed pool with predictable monthly billing. Grace, can you include a pricing sketch for 12-month reserved capacity vs a 3-month eval in the SOW draft?

Best,
Amanda
